summary: No new numbered sense is needed. The inherited inchoative gloss is widened to include the independently attested state meaning, rather than assigning another sense to Part act. or to a different experiencer.

Preterit Intransitive ṣahi/ṣahən/ṣahino/ṣahina can mark onset or a current resulting need for water. Part act. ṣahyo/ṣahye/ṣhiṯo predicates thirst as a state; ṣahyo wi shows a past state without turning the participle into Infectum-wa.
Human and animal experiencers are encoded as subjects; no stimulus object is attested. Environmental heat, walking and salt explain the state in context or in causal phrases.

ṣahwo is retained under the glossary’s Nomen Actionis label. Causal m-/me- marks death or difficulty from thirst, with an explicit excess construction in JTM 1.1/96; it is not an Infinitiv merely because it is non-finite.
The repeated Ṣahən at MAC NE TERTO ZARE/20 and the singular/plural parallel at 70/212 retain separate occurrence decisions; only the informative latter pair is quoted once.
The full PrS 70/18 text duplicates the inherited Part act. quotation, cited prs 198/11. Numbering concordance needs editorial verification rather than automatic recitation.

All three supplied tokens are I Part act. plural state predicates, not finite Preterit Intransitive or Infectum-wa. A past copula wayna locates a thirst state in the past; kfayši ṣahye expresses persistence.

Round 1 already filled Part act. sense 1 to five with singular, plural, past-state and feminine animal examples. Jan's thin-cell counts refer to the older entry; these routine examples add no missing form or meaning and are not repeated.

The full verse at Jan 2.5/1476 also has hawi ṣahwo with diminished springs and no water, suggesting environmental water shortage/drought as a nominal use. That does not establish a new finite ṣhy sense, and the nominal token was not separately supplied as an occurrence.
No special experiencer coding appears: thirsty persons are subjects or state bearers. No new idiom or light-verb construction is established.
Confirm the contracted feminine Ṣíṯono at MAC NE TERTO ZARE/21 against ṣhiṯo-no; do not silently restore h or classify it under ṣyṯ.
Verify the concordance between prs 198/11 and PrS 70/18 before changing the inherited reference.
For future reading runs, retain explicitly listed Nomen Actionis forms such as ṣahwo consistently; the present assignment includes and audits them.
At Jan 2.5/1476 does hawi ṣahwo specifically name drought, or a shared condition of thirst? Check the nominal lexical range separately from the verb before adding a numbered sense.
Jan has machine translations only; none is imported as edition text. No example addition is needed while the corresponding cell is full after round 1.

Ṣahye with wayna, with fyš, and with ne independently supports the state meaning already added to the gloss in round 1. Refugee families, abandoned children and monastery residents remain ordinary human thirst experiencers.
